lines.text: What's the smallest n that makes the sum a multiple of two thousand twenty-four?
lines.caption: What's the smallest n that makes the sum a multiple of two thousand twenty-four?

lines.text: The sum is half of n times n plus one.
lines.caption: The sum is half of n times n plus one.

lines.text: So n times n plus one needs sixteen, eleven and twenty-three.
lines.caption: So n times n plus one needs sixteen, eleven and twenty-three.

lines.text: Here's the trick. Neighbors share no factors, so each goes whole into one of them.
lines.caption: Here's the trick. Neighbors share no factors, so each goes whole into one of them.

lines.text: Sort them into two boxes, and check the multiples.
lines.caption: Sort them into two boxes, and check the multiples.

lines.text: Five hundred twenty-eight and five hundred twenty-nine fit perfectly.
lines.caption: Five hundred twenty-eight and five hundred twenty-nine fit perfectly.

lines.text: So n is five hundred twenty-eight: Choice C!
